# `scope_speed_move`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start, update or stop a continuous manual move of the mount along a direction at a given speed.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build: C / MUTATOR established independently, full contract parity unresolved) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x7d9f0 (64-bit guider build); axis command helper @0x68870; repeat worker @0x6a0e0; movement-limit worker CheckMoveLimit @0x6dc60, SendAlert @0x6d9a0; 32-bit handler @0x73d30 |

Requires a connected mount that supports it. A nonzero move stores the shared move parameters (change time, angle, duration, speed) and starts, or updates, a repeat worker that sends the axis speed and timed-move commands; the reply is sent when the worker has been started, long before motion ends, and the handler does not branch on the start result. Repeated requests update the same shared parameters. A request whose effective speed is below 0.01 in magnitude (or percent below 0.01) is an immediate stop: it sends zero speeds on both axes and polls for up to roughly 1000 ms before replying with result 0. No completion event exists for this method. The repeat worker also starts a movement-limit worker that polls the controller status; when the controller reports an axis limit it asks the imager to play a warning sound, emits a guider Alert event with code 532 (upper limit), 533 (lower limit), 540 or 541 (both with the fallback text fail to operate), and waits about 3 s before checking again. The limit geometry is controller-defined (INFERRED). A client SHOULD stop the move when it receives one of these alerts. Speeds are written raw to the controller as its native rate value (per-axis clamp 1440); the physical unit is unresolved (needs a device test). Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): :Rv<d or r> axis rate, then a timed move or :MTD<dir>; speed is clamped to 1440 and below 0.01 becomes an abort.

Side effects: Writes shared move parameters, starts or controls the repeat-move and movement-limit workers and sends axis speed and timed-move commands to the mount controller; a stop sends zero speeds. At an axis limit the limit worker asks the imager to play a sound and emits Alert (532, 533, 540 or 541).

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_speed_move"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Named object only: the parameter map does not bind positional names. Request a stop with a percent below 0.01 (for example 0). Native clamp after parsing: an axis speed with magnitude above 1440 is replaced by 1440, and with the anti-resonance option (used by the repeat worker) magnitudes in 900..1000 inclusive are snapped to 899 (up to 950) or 1001 (above 950). [READ] |
| `params.speed` | number | if percent is absent | - | Optional direct speed in the mount's native motor-speed units (a protocol multiplier, not proven to be degrees per second). If present and numeric it takes precedence over percent and is used as the base speed; otherwise percent is required. Its absolute value is used; an absolute value below 0.01 selects the immediate-stop branch. Not emitted by the Android app. [READ] |
| `params.percent` | number | if speed is absent | - | Speed as a percentage. Below 0.01 selects the immediate-stop branch (angle, level and dur_sec are then not read). Otherwise the base speed is 1440*percent/100 when level > 0, or 64*percent/100 when level <= 0 (multiplied by the guider's speed-move ratio when that ratio exceeds 0.01). No range check or clamp in the handler; the native per-axis clamp below applies later. Integer or real accepted. [READ] |
| `params.level` | integer | if percent >= 0.01 and speed is absent | - | Speed scale selector: > 0 uses the 1440 scale, <= 0 the 64 scale (see percent). Must be an integer. [READ] |
| `params.angle` | integer | if not an immediate stop | - | Direction in degrees. The axis speeds are cos(angle)*speed and sin(angle)*speed. Zero point and rotation sense of the angle relative to the sky or the mount axes are unresolved. No range check. [READ] |
| `params.dur_sec` | integer | if not an immediate stop | - | Duration passed to the timed-move command field. Seconds are INFERRED from the field name; no local deadline conversion was found. No range check. The Android app sends 3. [READ (field); INFERRED (unit)] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 102 | Invalid parameters; two separate branches exist but their exact triggers are unresolved | `invalid params` |
| 104 | level, angle or dur_sec is required but missing or not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 203 | The mount is in a state that does not admit the move | `equipment is moving` |
| 210 | The mount or its driver does not support the move | `not supported` |
| 315 | No mount is connected | `mount is not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

A missing or non-numeric percent (with no numeric speed) is rejected by a parameter branch whose code is not separately established. Further branches forward an error code set by the mount driver or a helper; the codes are not exhausted by this table.

## Example

Request, move - Move shape as the app sends it (values invented):

```json
{"id":41,"method":"scope_speed_move","params":{"percent":50,"angle":90,"level":1,"dur_sec":3}}
```

Request, stop - Immediate stop:

```json
{"id":42,"method":"scope_speed_move","params":{"percent":0}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_speed_move","result":0,"code":0,"id":41}
```

Reply, no-mount:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_speed_move","error":"mount is not connected","code":315,"id":43}
```
